newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela's Matos sees stable forex rate in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela's Matos sees stable forex rate in 1997.

text.p: Venezuela's local currency, which has come under greater pressure in recent weeks, will remain broadly stable during the remainder of 1997, Finance Minister Luis Raul Matos Azocar said Monday.

"There is no chance of a sharp jump in the exchange rate due to the (foreign) reserves situation," Matos told Union Radio. Venezuela's foreign reserves stood at $16.343 billion on July 21, according to the Central Bank.
After depreciating just 2.5 percent in the first half of the year, the bolivar has weakened a further percentage point in recent weeks to around 494 bolivars per dollar.
At the start of 1997, the Central Bank set a central parity of 472 bolivars per dollar with maximum and minimum limits 7.5 percent either side.
The central parity was set to depreciate at a monthly rate of 1.32 percent, in line with the government 1997 inflation target of 30 to 35 percent.
Despite its recent slide, Matos said, the bolivar remains within the Central Bank's limits and had come under pressure due largely to a bubble of excess liquidity in money markets.
The Central Bank would begin issuing treasury bills on behalf of the government in the first week of August as a new tool to soak up the excess liquidity, he added.
